newsitem.title: MAURITANIA: Toxic algae kill rare monk seals off Mauritania.
newsitem.headline: Toxic algae kill rare monk seals off Mauritania.

text.p: The bodies of 36 rare monk seals, apparently the victims of toxic algae, have washed up on the Mauritanian coast, the national oceanographic and fisheries research centre said on Saturday.

A baby monk seal, one of the world's most endangered species, was rescued and is recovering in the centre's aquarium in Nouadhibou. Dutch and Spanish marine scientists are investigating the cause of the deaths.

Some 150 monk seals of a world total of about 350 live off Mauritania, Western Sahara and Morocco. So called because folds of skin around their necks recall monastic dress, they are among the last members of the seal family living in temperate waters in the northern hemisphere.
They are under threat from viral infections, from pollution and fishing which deplete their feeding grounds, and from fishermen who kill them because they damage nets and eat fish.
A baby monk seal which had apparently lost her parents in a storm was treated at the centre and released back into the sea in January 1996.
